raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer cache writes when a prefill chunk starts inside a pool. Recover missing members from the request's existing tail before reseeding it. Fixes #63168.

## Claims

- Write complete pools at all chunk-start residues, including chunks shorter than a pool and a request following another prefill in the batch.
- Preserve the existing compression, Hadamard/FP8 quantization, cache layout, scheduler and decode writers.
- Share the strided gather between CUDA/ROCm and register compile-only startup warmup; metadata offset views do not add a new runtime-JIT variant.

## Validation

[Public evidence bundle](https://gist.github.com/Loken-Lau/520b35aa7201bd528e1f6da7752820a1): reproduction scripts, original/fixed logs, benchmark samples, controlled output diagnostics and profiler traces. All experiments below were actually run. The source patch contains seven files; experimental sorting/forcing hooks are outside the patch.

**2026-10-27 refresh:** rebased to main `90309f6b742cdb1d6305778b81063918cf61be81`, head `c08c802af19a7a6e4d03d17068f29a692faad941`; `git range-diff` reports the same functional patch. With compatible current wheel assets, H200 reruns pass the full kernel file **81 / 1 ROCm skip** and full GLM directory **35 / 8 ROCm skips**, including upstream's new KDA refit tests. The unchanged real-LLM observer checks 6 pools, 2 unaligned boundaries, 0 mismatches. Local SM80 passes 22 / 21 capability skips; applicable pre-commit hooks and remote DCO pass. `SYNC_2026-10-27.md` and new raw logs in the evidence bundle document the wheel compatibility check and resolved stale-binary/setup failures. Earlier benchmark/output-control measurements below remain October 24 experiments, not new performance claims.

H200 NVL, Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Triton 3.8.0; TP1. Real checkpoint `JaredforReal/GLM-5.3-Flash-4L`, pinned revision `035b309e03a83deb2589d722ddf9e3c5d3de5caf`. The checkpoint retains original widths/weights for three KDA layers and one DSA/MoE layer, but its model card says generated language is meaningless. These are production-path/cache and output-control experiments, **not full-checkpoint language-quality evaluation**.

| Check | Original | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New 48-case native-indexer regression | 28 failed / 20 passed for cache-byte mismatches | All 48 pass |
| Whole kernel test file | New regression run on base | 81 passed / 1 existing ROCm-only skip |
| Public `LLM` regression, budget 2045, two 4807/4808-token inputs | Two boundary pools each differ by 130 bytes | Six observed pools, two unaligned boundaries, zero mismatches |
| Full GLM test directory | Not rerun as a full base suite | 32 passed / 8 ROCm-only skips |
| Metadata-offset JIT regression | Removing only the alignment annotation fails under the error-mode JIT monitor | Same assertions pass with it |
| Compute Sanitizer on all new native cases | Not a logic oracle | 48 passed / zero memory errors |

Reproduction on a supported CUDA Hopper/Blackwell GPU with the pinned model available:

```bash
export PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH
export GLM5_PRUNED_MODEL=/path/to/glm5next-4l
export GLM5_TEST_GPU_UTIL=0.45  # shared H200; test default is 0.9
export VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -rs tests/models/glm5next
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -rs tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py
compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --error-exitcode 99 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py -k chunked_prefill
```

Additional gather oracle/graph-replay checks pass 32 cases across local A100/A800 and 16 on H200; eight finite bit-pattern cases include signed zero/subnormals. The full local SM80 model folder passes 19 with 21 capability skips. All applicable pre-commit hooks pass, including mypy, ruff, test tethering and markdownlint. Normal MkDocs build and generated HTML/navigation/search checks pass with existing warnings retained; strict build is not claimed.

Writer GPU timings use CUPTI, CUDA graph and cold L2 after correctness checks and 25 warmups, one A/B/B/A order with two independent processes per arm. They cover the production wrapper's GPU work; graph replay excludes Python dispatch/CPU allocation overhead. Values are the two process medians:

| Prefill tokens | Original, μs | Fixed, μs | Writer speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 128 | 20.672 / 20.737 | 5.056 / 5.088 | 4.08× |
| 2048 | 33.280 / 33.313 | 9.153 / 9.217 | 3.63× |
| 8192 | 76.481 / 76.449 | 22.113 / 22.144 | 3.46× |

The 2048-token profile changes from 11 kernels to 2. This is a writer measurement, not a model acceleration claim. The official `vllm bench latency` control uses two 4808-token inputs, 8 outputs, eager, max sequences 1 and budget 2048; fixed NumPy/engine seeds, A/B/B/A, 3 warmups + 30 timed calls/process (**60 samples/version**). Pooled median: **0.303668 s original / 0.304363 s fixed (+0.229%)**; observed ranges 0.299674–0.313874 / 0.299336–0.329979 s. Shared GPU, unlocked clocks. No demonstrated whole-model acceleration or statistical equivalence. The standard-entry script and all samples are in the evidence bundle.

<details>
<summary>Output variation, graph/JIT and synchronization controls</summary>

An earlier uninstrumented control has one divergent sequence (381/384 paired token positions exact). It is retained rather than classified as exact equality. The unchanged upstream `check_logprobs_close` passes with one mismatch warning.

Follow-up same-engine controls keep the first five decoded tokens fixed and switch only the exact original/fixed prefill writer. Four rounds compare **461568 aligned prefill pools with zero cache-byte mismatches**. The original writer also reproduces the same sixth-token flip (initial round 2/64 original, 4/64 fixed; detailed round 1/64 original, 0/64 fixed); these are diagnostics, not estimates of equal flip rates.

Direct observation keeps all 1203 pool scores and the selected set of 512 pools identical; all 64 selected-score multisets match the reference, but their return order varies. The cutoff is unique, so this is not a changed cutoff selection. Fixing only the probe's returned order, preserving its set/scores, makes every captured stage and all **154880 vocabulary logits bit-exact across 64 original/fixed repeats**. This isolates order-dependent downstream numerical variation in that workload; the production patch changes neither top-k selection nor ordering and does not include the sorting/forcing hooks. Raw score/order hashes and layer observations are retained.

Non-eager serving was tested using actual graph execution statistics: both versions report 28 FULL / 20 NONE executions across warmup plus three calls. This architecture intentionally uses `CompilationMode.NONE` with breakable graphs and existing compiled leaves; full-model FX/Inductor compilation is not claimed. Startup warmup changes from 23 keys/4 wrappers to 24/5. The new gather produces no additional runtime-JIT event after registration; three existing events remain in both versions.

Full-engine `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` fails in both versions at the same existing FlashInfer unpinned CPU-to-GPU metadata copy. Those failures remain disclosed. The changed writer separately passes the armed checker for 100 calls at each of n=0/1/3/128/2048/8192; an `.item()` positive control is rejected.

</details>

## Details

Previously, pool members were gathered from preceding rows of the current batch and its leading rows were masked. At an unaligned start, some members belong to the preceding chunk. Depending on batch placement, the completed pool was skipped or used another request's rows.

The shared gather accepts a batch member only if both absolute position and tail-block ownership agree; otherwise it reads that request's ring slot. It uses real tail capacity/strides, masks invalid slots, and runs before the existing tail seed. Calls without tail metadata retain the aligned fallback. No host tensor reads or data-dependent synchronization are added to this path. Startup warmup uses the existing compile-only dispatcher and bound cache metadata; it allocates no real warmup tensors. Scalar metadata pointers are not alignment-specialized; data pointers retain specialization.

The kernel regression covers all four start residues, chunks of 1/3/12, first/later request placement and 4-slot/16-slot padded tails through real metadata/context and production indexers. The public LLM test observes the real production writer through hooks and independent pool assembly; it does not replace model methods or metadata. The JIT-monitor test is process-isolated.

**Native ROCm numerical/graph execution remains pending AMD CI.** Offline compilation of the actual gather succeeds for 16 combinations of gfx942/gfx950, ring 4/16, BF16/FP32 scores and feature stride 1/2; this is explicitly not runtime evidence. Existing B200/MI355 native-kernel and GLM model jobs select the affected tests. An eligible upstream maintainer/trusted contributor must trigger pre-approval AMD CI; new fork commits do not start it automatically. TP>1, real PD/MTP acceptance and full-checkpoint quality are also not claimed tested.

Post-submission checks: DCO passes. Upstream `pre-run-check` stops on contributor eligibility (1 merged PR; 4 or a qualifying label required), so remote pre-commit does not run. Read the Docs build 35376482 stops at the same prerequisite before MkDocs. Local pre-commit and normal MkDocs results above are not represented as successful remote CI. No eligibility label has been requested.

Pre-submission duplicate checks covered issue discussion, all-state number/unaligned-keyword searches and actual related PR diffs. Both searches returned no PR for this fix. #57161 optimizes this writer but lacked prior-tail boundary recovery; #57537 provides general pruned-checkpoint coverage. Original experiments use base `e9acf48614a2c0d027d7aa2f0e38d963117617a6`; the first submission was based on `1bd56eaef38d0db35852fc38932d0c63003ef9f1`. The October 27 rebase preserves the same patch; the NVIDIA file also incorporates main's unrelated DCP interleave-property cleanup. Source hashes and the equivalent `range-diff` are retained with the refresh evidence.

**AI assistance:** Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, tests and experiments. The human requester confirmed review of this patch and authorized the additional validation and publication. The reported test commands were executed by Codex at that request; they are not represented as personally executed by the human. A public evidence bundle backs the claims and records the limitations.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -79,6 +79,15 @@ llm = LLM(model="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct", max_num_batched_tokens=16384
 
 See related papers for more details (<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.08671> or <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.16369>).
 
+### GLM-5.3-Flash Kpool Indexer
+
+GLM-5.3-Flash's compressed sparse attention indexer supports chunked prefill
+boundaries within a pool. The indexer combines tokens from the current chunk
+with that request's cached tail before updating the tail for the next step.
+No extra option is required, and `max_num_batched_tokens` does not need to be
+a multiple of the indexer's pool size. This also applies when decode requests
+leave a prefill budget that is not pool-aligned.
+
 ## Parallelism Strategies
 
 vLLM supports multiple parallelism strategies that can be combined to optimize performance across different hardware configurations.

@@ -63,6 +63,159 @@ def _make_caches():
     return kv, tail
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("start_remainder", range(4))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("chunk_size", [1, 3, 12])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("preceding_request", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ring_size,padding", [(4, 0), (16, 64)])
+def test_chunked_prefill_uses_its_own_pool_history(
+    start_remainder: int,
+    chunk_size: int,
+    preceding_request: bool,
+    ring_size: int,
+    padding: int,
+):
+    """Chunk boundaries must not drop pools or mix different requests' keys."""
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.forward_context import set_forward_context
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.indexer import (
+        DeepseekV32IndexerMetadata,
+        DeepseekV32IndexerPrefillMetadata,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import init_workspace_manager
+
+    if current_platform.is_rocm():
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.sparse_indexer import (
+            sparse_attn_indexer_kpool,
+        )
+    else:
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.sparse_indexer import (
+            sparse_attn_indexer_kpool,
+        )
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    pool = 4
+    start = 32 + start_remainder
+    end = start + chunk_size
+    key = torch.randn(48, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    score = torch.randn_like(key)
+    ape = torch.randn(pool, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    kv, tail = _make_caches()
+    tail = torch.empty_strided(
+        (NUM_BLOCKS, 2, ring_size, HEAD_DIM),
+        (2 * ring_size * HEAD_DIM + padding, ring_size * HEAD_DIM, HEAD_DIM, 1),
+        dtype=tail.dtype,
+        device=tail.device,
+    ).zero_()
+    expected = kv.clone()
+    prior_pos = torch.arange(start, device="cuda")
+    kpool_seed_tail_cache(
+        tail,
+        key[:start],
+        score[:start],
+        ring_size + prior_pos % ring_size,
+        pool,
+        HEAD_DIM,
+    )
+
+    positions = torch.arange(start, end, device="cuda")
+    slots = torch.where(positions % pool == pool - 1, positions // pool, -1)
+    tail_slots = ring_size + positions % ring_size
+    batch_key, batch_score = key[start:end], score[start:end]
+    first_pool, last_pool = start // pool, end // pool
+    if last_pool > first_pool:
+        kpool_compress_and_write_cache(
+            expected,
+            key[first_pool * pool : last_pool * pool].reshape(-1, pool, HEAD_DIM),
+            score[first_pool * pool : last_pool * pool].reshape(-1, pool, HEAD_DIM),
+            ape,
+            torch.arange(first_pool, last_pool, device="cuda"),
+            pool,
+            HEAD_DIM,
+        )
+
+    if preceding_request:
+        prior_key = torch.randn(12, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        prior_score = torch.randn_like(prior_key)
+        prior_positions = torch.arange(12, device="cuda")
+        prior_slots = torch.where(
+            prior_positions % pool == pool - 1, 64 + prior_positions // pool, -1
+        )
+        kpool_compress_and_write_cache(
+            expected,
+            prior_key.reshape(-1, pool, HEAD_DIM),
+            prior_score.reshape(-1, pool, HEAD_DIM),
+            ape,
+            torch.arange(64, 67, device="cuda"),
+            pool,
+            HEAD_DIM,
+        )
+        positions = torch.cat((prior_positions, positions))
+        slots = torch.cat((prior_slots, slots))
+        tail_slots = torch.cat(
+            (2 * ring_size + prior_positions % ring_size, tail_slots)
+        )
+        batch_key = torch.cat((prior_key, batch_key))
+        batch_score = torch.cat((prior_score, batch_score))
+
+    n = len(positions)
+    metadata = DeepseekV32IndexerMetadata(
+        seq_lens=torch.tensor(
+            [12, end] if preceding_request else [end],
+            device="cuda",

+            (t // ring, pos): i
+            for i, (t, pos) in enumerate(zip(tail_slots, positions))
+            if t >= 0

+        for pos, slot, ts in zip(positions, slots, tail_slots):
+            if slot < 0 or ts < 0 or ts // ring in chosen:
+                continue
+            block = ts // ring
+            chosen.add(block)
+            start = min(p for b, p in lookup if b == block)
+            report["starts"].append(start)
+            report["unaligned"] += int(start % pool != 0)
+            ks, ss = [], []
+            for member in range(pos - pool + 1, pos + 1):
+                src = lookup.get((block, member))
+                if src is None:
+                    ks.append(mod.tail_cache.kv_cache[block, 0, member % ring])
+                    ss.append(mod.tail_cache.kv_cache[block, 1, member % ring])

+    def post(mod, inputs, kwargs, output):
+        for slot, want, start, pos in mod.kpool_prefill_pending:
+            cache = mod.k_cache.kv_cache
+            page, offset = divmod(slot, cache.shape[1])
+            flat = cache[page].reshape(-1)
+            got = torch.cat(
+                (
+                    flat[offset * 128 : (offset + 1) * 128],
+                    flat[
+                        cache.shape[1] * 128 + 4 * offset : cache.shape[1] * 128
+                        + 4 * offset
+                        + 4
+                    ],
+                )
+            )

+            if not torch.equal(got, want):

+                        "completion": pos,
+                        "slot": slot,
+                        "different_bytes": int((got != want).sum()),

+            mod.register_forward_pre_hook(pre, with_kwargs=True)
+            mod.register_forward_hook(post, with_kwargs=True)
+            found += 1
